genZNote: Produces violacein, a deep purple pigment so striking that this organism is basically a walking microbiology demo — usually harmless, but capable of a nasty infection in the right (wrong) circumstances.

morphology.motility: Motile via one polar and several lateral flagella

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil and water in tropical and subtropical regions
habitat.hostAssociation: Free-living environmental organism; rare opportunistic pathogen in humans following wound contamination
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Widespread in warm freshwater and soil worldwide, especially in tropical climates

culture.colonyMorphology: Distinctive violet-black colonies from violacein pigment; some strains are non-pigmented
culture.pigmentation: Deep violet (violacein) in pigmented strains; pigmentation can be lost or reduced with temperature/strain variation

identificationClues: Striking violet-black colony pigmentation from violacein, one of the most visually distinctive pigments in clinical/environmental microbiology
Oxidase-positive Gram-negative rod, distinguishing it from most Enterobacterales
Rare but potentially fulminant opportunistic infections follow contamination of wounds with soil or stagnant water, especially in warm climates
Non-pigmented strains exist and can be misidentified without biochemical confirmation

diseases: Rare but severe soft-tissue infections, sepsis, and abscesses following wound contamination with contaminated soil/water
clinicalImportance.transmission: Environmental exposure — contamination of skin wounds with soil or stagnant fresh water, particularly in tropical/subtropical regions
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Uncommon but associated with high mortality when it does cause invasive disease, especially in immunocompromised hosts
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Violet pigmentation plus oxidase positivity is a strong presumptive identification clue

examFacts.importantDisease: Rare severe wound/soft-tissue infection or sepsis (tropical climates)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: One of the most visually distinctive pigment-producing bacteria; usually environmental but capable of severe opportunistic disease
